rics.meaning: Actual MoM percent change in US nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft — the 'core capex' proxy — from Census Bureau.
rics.how_to_use: Best single indicator for US business investment intentions; leads Industrial Production by 1-3 months. Sustained positive trend supports GDP upgrades and equity risk appetite.

rics.meaning: Median consensus forecast for nondefense capital goods ex-aircraft (core capex) MoM change from the Reuters pre-release poll.
rics.how_to_use: Benchmark for capex surprise; positive print vs median supports business investment narrative and leads Industrial Production revisions upward.

rics.meaning: Mean forecast for core capex MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median; outlier bullish capex views (M&A-driven equipment orders) can pull mean above median.

rics.meaning: Mode forecast for core capex MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Tight mode-median alignment confirms consensus on business investment trend; wide gap flags analyst disagreement about capex cycle phase.

rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for core capex MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines bearish capex scenario; print below min signals capex contraction that may prompt downward GDP tracking revisions.

rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for core capex MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines bullish capex scenario; print above max indicates broad investment acceleration, typically supportive of industrial and tech equities.

rics.description: Nondefe Cap Ex-Air — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of core capex MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Elevated StdDev preceding a cycle turn (recession or recovery) is typical; monitor alongside GDPNow capex tracker for consistency.

rics.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for core capex (nondefense cap goods ex-air) MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median to detect model-driven capex signal; macro model inputs (ISM Capital Goods, PPI metals) often lead analyst surveys on this series.

rics.meaning: Predicted surprise for core capex (nondefense capital goods ex-air) MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Key pre-release risk gauge for business investment tone; strong positive predicted surprise alongside rising ISM Capex is a GDP growth signal.

rics.description: Nondefe Cap Ex-Air — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists submitting a core capex forecast in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Core capex typically draws fewer respondents than headline durables; low count reduces statistical reliability of median and mean.

rics.description: Nondef Cap Ex-Air R MM — Actual
rics.meaning: Revised actual MoM percent change for nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft, published alongside the following month's advance release.
rics.how_to_use: Revision from the advance (USNDXA=ECI) captures order adjustments; compare advance vs revised to assess measurement noise and improve forecasting models.

rics.meaning: Census Bureau monthly actual MoM percent change in US durable goods orders (items intended to last 3+ years), released ~25-26th of the following month.
rics.how_to_use: Highly volatile due to aircraft/defense swings; use Ex-Transport (USDGXT=ECI) for trend. Upside surprises lift cyclicals and USD.

rics.meaning: Median consensus forecast for the MoM change in US durable goods orders from the Reuters pre-release poll.
rics.how_to_use: Headline durable goods is noisy; track deviation from median alongside Ex-Transport median to distinguish underlying trend from transport volatility.

rics.meaning: Mean forecast for durable goods orders MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median to detect skew from outlier forecasters; outlier large Boeing orders sometimes pull mean well above median.

rics.meaning: Mode (most common) forecast for durable goods orders MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Mode clustering near zero indicates consensus expects a flat month; significant deviation from median signals split views on transport orders.

rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for durable goods orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the bearish bound; actual print below min indicates an extreme negative surprise, typically negative for industrial/cyclical equities.

rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for durable goods orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the bullish bound; Boeing large-order months can produce prints well above max, which tend to be followed by mean-reversion next month.

rics.meaning: Standard deviation of durable goods orders forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: High StdDev reflects uncertainty about aircraft/defense swing factor; compare with Ex-Transport StdDev to isolate volatility source.

rics.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for durable goods orders MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median (=M) to flag potential non-consensus signal; useful for assessing whether model factors (PMI, ISM) confirm or diverge from analyst consensus.

rics.meaning: Predicted surprise for durable goods orders — SmartEconomics directional estimate of deviation from consensus at release.
rics.how_to_use: Use pre-release to gauge skew risk; combine with ISM Manufacturing New Orders as a directional cross-check.

rics.meaning: Number of economists submitting a forecast for durable goods orders in the current Reuters poll cycle.
rics.how_to_use: Validate consensus reliability; low count ahead of releases following large Boeing announcements reflects forecaster uncertainty about transport component.

rics.meaning: Actual MoM percent change in US durable goods orders excluding volatile defense spending, from Census Bureau.
rics.how_to_use: Removes lumpy government contracts to reveal private-sector demand; compare with headline and Ex-Transport to triangulate underlying manufacturing momentum.

rics.meaning: Median consensus forecast for durable goods orders MoM change excluding defense orders from the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Use to separate private demand trends from government contract timing; persistent upside vs consensus indicates non-defense manufacturing recovery.

rics.meaning: Mean forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change across Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median to identify skew; outlier views on commercial aircraft can still distort mean even after defense exclusion.

rics.meaning: Mode forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Tight clustering of mode near median signals analyst consensus on underlying ex-defense trend; gaps indicate split views.

rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the bearish scenario for private manufacturing; useful for stress-testing capex outlooks when combined with core capex (USNDXA) range.

rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the bullish scenario; actual print above max indicates unexpected surge in private-sector capital goods demand.

rics.description: Durables Ex-Defense MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of durable goods ex-defense MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Lower StdDev vs headline durables confirms defense exclusion reduces forecast uncertainty; persistent high StdDev may reflect aircraft order uncertainty.

rics.meaning: SmartEconomics model forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median to check if macro models aligned on defense-stripped trend; useful when large DoD contracts distort headline consensus.

rics.meaning: Predicted surprise for durable goods ex-defense orders MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Signals pre-release surprise direction for private manufacturing demand; combine with ISM New Orders sub-index as a cross-check.

rics.description: Durables Ex-Defense MM — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of forecasters submitting an ex-defense durable goods estimate in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Typically lower response rate than headline durables; low count increases noise in consensus measures.

rics.meaning: Actual MoM percent change in US durable goods orders excluding transportation equipment (aircraft, autos), from Census Bureau.
rics.how_to_use: Preferred signal for underlying manufacturing demand since it strips Boeing batch effects; sustained positive trend indicates broad capex expansion.

rics.meaning: Median consensus forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change from the Reuters pre-release poll.
rics.how_to_use: Most watched durables sub-forecast by markets; positive surprise vs this median is the cleaner signal for industrial/capex sentiment compared to headline.

rics.meaning: Mean forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to check for outlier forecaster influence on the distribution of expectations for core manufacturing.

rics.meaning: Mode forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: When mode matches median, consensus is tightly formed; divergence signals forecaster disagreement on auto/machinery sub-component trends.

rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Bearish bound for core manufacturing; actual below min is a strong contraction signal that may weigh on industrial capex outlook.

rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Bullish bound for core manufacturing; print above max signals broad-based order strength and supports upward Industrial Production revisions.

rics.meaning: Standard deviation of durable goods ex-transport MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Benchmark uncertainty for core manufacturing; compare to headline StdDev to confirm that stripping transport reduces forecast variance.

rics.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median for model vs analyst divergence on core manufacturing trend; PMI/ISM inputs typically anchor this estimate.

rics.meaning: Predicted surprise for durable goods ex-transport MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Pre-release surprise gauge for core manufacturing demand; positive predicted surprise with ISM confirmation raises industrial equity and USD outlook.

rics.meaning: Number of economists submitting a durable goods ex-transport forecast in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Higher participation than ex-defense given analyst focus on this strip; validate consensus quality, especially following supply-chain disruption periods.

rics.meaning: Census Bureau actual MoM percent change in total US factory orders (durable + nondurable goods), released ~4 weeks after the reference month.
rics.how_to_use: Broader than durables alone; nondurable component (chemicals, food, petroleum) adds refinery and consumer goods cycle signals. Upside confirms manufacturing recovery.

rics.meaning: Median consensus forecast for US factory orders MoM change from the Reuters pre-release poll.
rics.how_to_use: Primary factory orders benchmark; surprise vs median typically drives industrials and materials equities. Cross-check with the durables advance release already known.

rics.meaning: Mean forecast for factory orders MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median; energy-price swings can pull nondurable orders outliers, creating mean-median skew in the forecast distribution.

rics.meaning: Mode forecast for factory orders MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Mode near zero indicates stable consensus; significant positive mode reflects shared view on nondurable rebound (e.g., petroleum orders recovery).

rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for factory orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines worst-case scenario for total manufacturing demand; actual below min signals broad-based weakness across durable and nondurable goods.

rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for factory orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines bullish case; print above max would indicate unexpected surge across both durable and nondurable orders, rare outside energy-price spikes.

rics.description: Factory Orders MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of factory orders MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Elevated StdDev typically driven by uncertainty in petroleum/chemicals orders; compare with durable goods StdDev to identify nondurable uncertainty component.

rics.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for factory orders MoM change.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median; model may incorporate petroleum-price and PMI signals that analyst surveys lag, especially for nondurable component.

rics.meaning: Predicted surprise for factory orders MoM change — SmartEconomics directional estimate of actual deviation from consensus.
rics.how_to_use: Use pre-release to size surprise risk for broad manufacturing; strongly positive predicted surprise supports cyclical equity rotation.

rics.description: Factory Orders MM — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists submitting a factory orders forecast in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Factory orders draws a moderate response rate; lower count than NFP or CPI polls — validate consensus size before trading the surprise.

rics.meaning: BLS monthly actual count of US job openings (JOLTS), released with ~6-week lag. Measures unfilled demand for labor across all industries.
rics.how_to_use: Pre-COVID baseline ~7M; peaked ~12M (2022); now ~8M. Rising openings signal tight labor supply and support Fed hawkishness; compare with quits and layoffs in the same release.

rics.meaning: Median consensus forecast for US JOLTS Job Openings from Reuters poll conducted ~1 week before BLS release.
rics.how_to_use: Primary benchmark for surprise calculation; positive surprise (actual > median) lifts short-dated Treasuries via Fed tightening expectations. Track alongside NFP and quits rate.

rics.meaning: Mean (average) of all surveyed economist forecasts for JOLTS Job Openings for the upcoming BLS release.
rics.how_to_use: Use with median (=M) to detect skew in the distribution; mean > median indicates upside outlier forecasts skewing expectations.

rics.meaning: Mode (most frequently submitted) forecast for JOLTS Job Openings among Reuters poll respondents.
rics.how_to_use: Mode near median confirms tight consensus clustering; large gap signals bi-modal forecast distribution and higher surprise risk.

rics.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) individual forecast for JOLTS Job Openings submitted in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the bearish tail of analyst expectations; actual print below min signals an extreme downside surprise with potential risk-off impact.

rics.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) individual forecast for JOLTS Job Openings submitted in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the bullish tail; actual print above max is an extreme upside surprise, typically hawkish for rates and bullish for USD.

rics.description: JOLTS Job Openings — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for JOLTS Job Openings across all Reuters poll respondents, measuring forecast dispersion.
rics.how_to_use: High StdDev ahead of release signals elevated uncertainty; wider dispersion increases options premium on rate-sensitive instruments around JOLTS day.

rics.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for JOLTS Job Openings, derived from macro factor inputs rather than surveyed economists.
rics.how_to_use: Compare vs median (=M) to detect systematic model bias; large divergence may signal non-consensus regime shift in labor demand.

rics.meaning: Predicted surprise for JOLTS Job Openings — SmartEconomics estimate of likely direction and magnitude of deviation from consensus.
rics.how_to_use: Use pre-release to position for surprise risk; a strongly positive predicted surprise combined with tight labor market context raises rate-hike odds.

rics.description: JOLTS Job Openings — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for JOLTS Job Openings in the Reuters poll for the current release cycle.
rics.how_to_use: Higher count improves reliability of median/mean; fewer than ~15 respondents makes the consensus less representative of street expectations.
